A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Evidential Neural Radiance Fields by the same authors. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and image-based figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and uncertainty results on LF, LLFF, and RobustNeRF, with per-scene repeated-run statistics, sensitivity analyses, and application experiments.

after.justification: v2 reports revised original benchmark results, per-scene repeated-run statistics, uncertainty analyses, and retained scene-cleaning and active-learning experiments.

M1.justification: The propagation equations, evidential formulation, and losses remain unchanged. However, v1 explicitly assigns uncertainty outputs to the view-independent density head, whereas v2 removes that statement and groups them with color in Equation (9). The PDFs do not establish whether this represents an architectural change or revised notation and documentation.

E1.justification: Both retain four LF scenes, eight LLFF scenes, four RobustNeRF scenes, and Phototourism qualitative examples, alongside scene cleaning and active learning. The revised analysis examples use scenes within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: BayesRays is removed from Table 1, Tables 4–7, and the supplementary qualitative comparisons. The numerical tables instead include explicit nerfacto reconstruction-baseline rows. Dropout, Normal, MoL, Ensembles, and DANE remain; the newly discussed ENeRF is not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 removes AUCE throughout the evaluation and substantially revises the reported regularization settings in Table 3, including Leaves from 1e-4 to 5. The explicit 5k/30k dataset budgets become an unspecified scene-based convergence rule. The training-size study changes from 5–50 LLFF views to 10–50 RobustNeRF views, and the sensitivity sweep also changes.

E4.justification: Two existing analyses are revised: training-size sensitivity moves from an LLFF example to Android in RobustNeRF, and regularization sensitivity moves from Android to Leaves. Their questions remain the same. The transient-object case study, uncertainty-source examples, and application analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 4 adds error bars to the training-size analysis, absent from v1 Figure 3, although their definition and plot-specific run count are unstated. Both versions retain three-run benchmark averages, per-scene standard deviations, and active-learning error bars; no increase in run count is established.

E6.justification: Scores across Table 1 and Tables 4–7 are broadly replaced. For example, Evidential RobustNeRF PSNR changes from 25.8585 to 26.2292. Evidential has the lowest NLL on all three datasets in v1, but only LLFF in v2; MoL leads LF and RobustNeRF. These accompany revised settings, so they are not established same-setting gains. Qualitative maps and analysis curves also change; Table 2 timings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The uncertainty definitions, propagation assumptions and proofs, and Student-t/NLL derivations are retained, with appendix Sections 7–8 becoming 8–9. The main-text restriction of gamma to [0,1] restates the existing bounded-color construction. Replacing 'voxel' with 'point' does not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: v2 removes the introduction's explicit claim to be the first framework quantifying both uncertainty types and emphasizes separate aleatoric and epistemic estimates. The central single-pass formulation, standardized-benchmark contribution, and broad state-of-the-art claims remain.

C2.justification: The revised scaling analysis attributes increasing AU to additional cluttered observations, replacing v1's stable-AU interpretation. v2 also attributes MoL's strong NLL to multimodal modeling. The deterministic-density limitation is retained in shortened form, while its detailed transient-failure explanation and several future-extension discussions are removed.

D1.justification: v1 promises code release upon acceptance; v2 provides a repository link and states that code is available. Table 3 updates the disclosed coefficients, while exact dataset training budgets and the explicit uncertainty-head assignment disappear. The nerfacto defaults, dropout settings, ensemble size, and A6000 timing information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of concurrent ENeRF and its point-level NIG-mixture approach, citing the mixture-NIG work, and adds a Phototourism reference. It removes the BayesRays related-work paragraph and Laplace-approximation reference, while retaining the BayesRays citation for the LF split. The broader research taxonomy remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 consistently replaces 'voxel' with 'point', tightens several paragraphs, adds an acknowledgment, and consolidates supplementary quantitative, qualitative, and discussion sections. The main section sequence and most explanatory text remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 4 becomes a reformatted, full-width opening Figure 1. The main qualitative comparison is recomposed, the training-size plot becomes two panels, and comparison tables and supplementary grids are reconfigured after metric and comparator removals. The sensitivity figure and transient-example placement are also revised.

improvement.justification: v2 improves access information and research positioning through the code link and acknowledgment of concurrent ENeRF. However, it removes calibration and BayesRays evidence, makes training budgets less explicit, and shortens substantive limitations. The revised results accompany changed settings and an unresolved uncertainty-head specification. These competing changes do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration from the PDFs alone.
